intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Desha County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: During our evaluation, nothing came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated May 20, 2026. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Reed
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Treasurer. Mayor and Treasurer Restricted Street Fund monies were used to pay for Water and Sewer Fund expenses of $2,058, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. §§ 26-79-104, 27-70-207.

cities.name: Tillar
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer General Fund disbursements exceeded appropriations by $13,128 (27%), in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-58- 203.

cities.name: Watson
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer During our examination of payroll, it was discovered the Mayor and payroll preparer's actual pay, approved by the city council, did not agree with the 2023 budget. Furthermore, the payroll preparer's salaries were under-reported on their 2023 W-2's and over-reported on their 2024 W-2's.
